<query>Lately, when I look in mirrors or at photos, it feels like there's another me just behind the glass, watching but separate. Could these mirror images be actual alternate selves slipping into our world? How would I even know if I met my real self or an impostor?</query>
<response>Tallyn, your experience touches on deep philosophical and psychological questions. The feeling of another self "behind the glass" might relate to reflections of your own psyche—perhaps unexplored aspects of your identity or creative consciousness. While science doesn’t confirm alternate selves slipping into our world, some theories in quantum physics (like the "many-worlds" interpretation) speculate about parallel realities. However, distinguishing a "real" self from an "impostor" is subjective. Consider reflecting on what this sensation means to you: Could it symbolize your artistic duality, a search for authenticity, or a metaphor for the observer effect in art? If it persists, journaling or discussing it with a therapist might help unpack its source. For now, embrace the mystery—after all, art often thrives in the liminal space between the known and the imagined.</response>
